title: Medical alcohol test
what: A doctor checks if there is alcohol in your body. You blow into a device, and sometimes give blood or urine. The doctor also does a short exam.
why: At the request of police or an employer, after a road accident, or at medical checks for drivers and workers.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; the breath result comes right away, blood or urine results later
tell_doctor: If you used an alcohol-based spray, mouthwash, or drops
If you have diabetes or lung disease

prepare.title: Mouth
prepare.text: For 15 to 20 minutes before the breath test, do not smoke, eat, or rinse with anything containing alcohol.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell the doctor everything you take.

bring: Your referral or report, if you were sent
steps: The doctor checks your ID and fills out a report
You have a short exam: blood pressure, pulse, speech, and balance
You breathe out long and steady into a single-use mouthpiece
The breath test is usually repeated after 15 to 20 minutes
Sometimes blood from a vein or urine is taken for the lab
The doctor writes up the result
feel: You need to blow steadily and for a long time into the device
after: The breath result shows right away
Blood or urine results usually come in a few days
The official report is issued by the rules. Ask who gets it and when

faq.q: Can kvass or kefir show up as alcohol?
faq.a: Right after drinking, they can sometimes give very small numbers. That is why the breath test is repeated after 15 to 20 minutes.
That depends on the law in your country, and refusing can have consequences. Ask a lawyer or the officer who sent you.

reminders.text: Alcohol test soon. For 15 to 20 minutes before the breath test, do not smoke, eat, or rinse your mouth.
